requirements.heading: Unintended SMTP Client Failures
requirements.text: o Alternate (MX) servers SHOULD share the same greylisting database.

requirements.heading: Unintended SMTP Client Failures
requirements.text: o When alternate MX servers relay mail back to the "primary" MX server, the latter SHOULD be configured to permit the other servers to relay mail without being subjected to greylisting.

requirements.heading: Recommendations
requirements.text: The following practices are RECOMMENDED based on collected experience:

requirements.heading: Recommendations
requirements.text: The default range SHOULD be from one minute to 24 hours.

requirements.heading: Recommendations
requirements.text: Retries after the end of the range SHOULD be considered to be a new message for the purposes of greylisting evaluation (i.e., reset the "first seen" timestamp for that IP address).

requirements.heading: Recommendations
requirements.text: The default SHOULD be at least one week.

requirements.heading: Recommendations
requirements.text: For an Administrative Management Domain (ADMD), all inbound border MTAs listed in the [DNS] SHOULD share a common greylisting database and common greylisting policies.

requirements.heading: Recommendations
requirements.text: To accommodate those senders that have clusters of outgoing mail servers, greylisting servers MAY track CIDR blocks of a size of its own choosing, such as /24, rather than the full IPv4 address.

requirements.heading: Recommendations
requirements.text: (Note, however, that this heuristic will not work for clusters having machines on different networks.) A similar grouping capability MAY be established based on the domain name of the mail server if one can be determined.

requirements.heading: Recommendations
requirements.text: There are also some highly visible online entities such as email service providers that will be certain to retry; thus, those that are known SHOULD be allowed to bypass the filter.

requirements.heading: Recommendations
requirements.text: Greylisting SHOULD NOT be applied by an ADMD's submission service (see [SUBMISSION]) for authenticated client hosts.

requirements.heading: Recommendations
requirements.text: It also SHOULD not be applied against any authenticated ADMD session.
